original_question: Is the class of lattices that are isomorphic to a sublattice of the lattice of subgroups of some Abelian group a variety?
target_in_paper: Section 2, Problem 40: "Is the class of lattices that are isomorphic to a sublattice of the lattice of subgroups of some Abelian group a variety?"

missing_details: To make it fully stand-alone, spell out that 'variety' is meant in the universal-algebraic sense for lattices, i.e. an equationally axiomatizable class in the lattice operations meet and join; the notebook explicitly gives this gloss for the parallel nearby Problem 35.
Make the existential quantifier explicit: for a lattice L, there must exist an Abelian group G such that L is lattice-isomorphic to a sublattice of the subgroup lattice Sub(G).

refined_question: Let K be the class of all lattices L for which there exists an Abelian group G such that L is lattice-isomorphic to a sublattice of the subgroup lattice Sub(G). Is K a variety of lattices, that is, is K definable by a set of lattice identities in the language {meet, join}?
